note: About as close to the stated ICP as this corpus gets. Founding partner of his own law firm after seven years at a US firm's Slovak branch — 'successful' and 'income' are both unambiguous, and he accepted $6,000 with zero resistance or negotiation. 'Neglected_health' is the literal description of his case: 22 years in which work always won and health was the one thing that got no attention, with no crisis attached. 'Not_deconditioned' holds — he is not the excluded 50-lb-overweight gym-averse profile, he manages his diet without difficulty and says 'I'm not afraid of physical work or workout'. The one soft miss is 'good_to_great': he is restoring a former athletic self rather than taking an already-good position to great, and the honest framing of his starting point is winded-on-the-office-stairs. That is closer to rebuild than to optimisation. Scored 'core' regardless because he meets four of five criteria squarely and the fifth is a matter of degree, not of kind — but it is worth logging that the ICP's 'good to great' language keeps mis-describing the actual buyer, who is repeatedly a successful professional recovering ground rather than extending an advantage.
